old_problem: The OEM command has unexplained `-m5 5`, the literal address is unbound, and the procedure allows either DC cycle or warm reboot even though these have different state effects. It also clears bad-page and log evidence before the acceptance trail is sealed.
disposition_reason: Pending must remain. The extra positional 5 can change proprietary amdgpuras parsing and neither EDs nor public platform standards can authoritatively correct it. ED-06/18/20 also forbid choosing DC cycle and warm reboot interchangeably. All other aspects are parameterized, but executing or finalizing the command/recovery oracle still requires AMD/FAE/test-owner evidence.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2089, same-row DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record, unique-code result and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2090 / Wistron-AMD SVM-00134-V003 / bf211afa1ce74f1b was directly read from XLSX and manifest.
`-m5 5` is not validly reducible to `-m5`; deleting or reinterpreting the second 5 would invent proprietary CLI semantics.
The fixed address 0x800000000 requires signed device/OAM/UMC ownership and exclusion of OS/active/data allocations before injection.
The ext15 End-to-end CRC Deferred oracle is explicit and is preserved independently from bad-page cleanup.
Bad-page clear changes persistent evidence and must occur only after complete CPER/bad-page artifacts are sealed under a separate approval.
DC cycle and warm reboot are distinct coverage and recovery actions; one exact owner-selected path and its OFF/ON/OS-ready or reboot-ready oracle are required.
No amdgpuras, address probe, CPER, clear, reboot, cycle, recovery, log clear, retry or DUT action was performed.
